## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on this case and on the meaning of the test. None is used in this draft.
- Later commentators gave many accounts of what the test was; none is in the ayat and none is used here. A scholar should decide how the page should word the phrase that Dawud thought We had tested him (zanna anna-ma fatannahu).
- On etiquette, this draft gives no verdict on Dawud; it states what the ayat state, that he asked forgiveness and was forgiven.

## 1. The case and the test  (`#the-case-and-the-test`)

Cited ayat: 38:21-25

> **38:21** وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُا۟ ٱلْخَصْمِ إِذْ تَسَوَّرُوا۟ ٱلْمِحْرَابَ
>
> **38:22** إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ دَاوُۥدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ خَصْمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعْضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا تُشْطِطْ وَٱهْدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ
>
> **38:23** إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِى لَهُۥ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً وَلِىَ نَعْجَةٌ وَٰحِدَةٌ فَقَالَ أَكْفِلْنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِى فِى ٱلْخِطَابِ
>
> **38:24** قَالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ ٱلْخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبْغِى بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلٌ مَّا هُمْ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّ رَاكِعًا وَأَنَابَ
>
> **38:25** فَغَفَرْنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَـَٔابٍ

### Claims

**c1** (38:21): The ayah asks whether the news of the disputants has reached the hearer, when they climbed into the mihrab.

**c2** (38:22): They entered upon Dawud and he was alarmed at them; they said: do not fear, we are a pair of disputants, one of us has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth, do not be unjust, and guide us to the right path.

**c3** (38:23): One of them said: this is my brother, he has ninety-nine ewes and I have one ewe; he said to entrust it to him, and he overcame me in speech.

**c4** (38:24): Dawud said: he has wronged you by asking for your ewe to add to his ewes; many partners wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they.

**c5** (38:24): Dawud thought that We had tested him; he asked forgiveness of his Lord, fell down bowing, and turned to God.

**c6** (38:25): God forgave him that, and said that he has nearness to Us and a good place of return.

### One-minute summary

A pair of disputants came to Dawud with a case about one ewe and ninety-nine ewes, and Dawud gave judgement [c2][c3][c4]. Dawud thought that he had been tested, asked forgiveness, fell down bowing and turned to God, and God forgave him [c5][c6].

### Complete story

The ayah asks whether the news of the disputants has reached the hearer, when they climbed into the mihrab [c1]. They entered upon Dawud and he was alarmed at them [c2]. They said: do not fear, we are a pair of disputants, one of us has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth, do not be unjust, and guide us to the right path [c2].

One of them said: this is my brother, he has ninety-nine ewes and I have one ewe; he said to entrust it to him, and he overcame me in speech [c3]. Dawud said: he has wronged you by asking for your ewe to add to his ewes; many partners wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they [c4].

Dawud thought that We had tested him; he asked forgiveness of his Lord, fell down bowing, and turned to God [c5]. God forgave him that, and said that he has nearness to Us and a good place of return [c6].

### Deep study

Dawud's answer speaks of partners in general and then names the exceptions, those who believe and do righteous deeds [c4]. The ayah does not say what Dawud was forgiven; it says only that God forgave him that [c5][c6]. The same ayah that gives his judgement gives his turning to God, so the case and the test are told together [c4][c5].

### Kids mode

A pair of people came to Dawud with an argument about sheep: one had ninety-nine and the other had one [c2][c3]. Dawud gave his answer, then asked God to forgive him and bowed down, and God forgave him [c4][c5][c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the case teaches that many who share a thing wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds [c4]. Another is that the passage ends with turning to God and with forgiveness [c5][c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the disputants were, whether they were people or something else, or how they entered; the ayah says only that they climbed into the mihrab.
- Not established: what Dawud thought was the test, or what he was forgiven; the ayah says that without naming it.
- Not established: whether the case is a real dispute or a parable; the ayah does not say.
- Not established: where or when this was, or what Dawud did after the judgement.
